# bee

> bee is an open-source coding agent harness written in Go. It gives an LLM tools to edit code, run tests and commit changes. Installation provides one static binary. Skills can be invoked directly as `bee <name>`.

Use Ollama or oMLX for local inference, with no API keys or provider rate limits. Prompts and code stay on your machine. Hosted options include OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini. Author: Henry Schober. Source and issues: https://github.com/elhenro/bee

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elhenro/bee/main/README.md): overview, install, quickstart, configuration
- [Go API reference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/elhenro/bee): exported packages and types, rendered from godoc
- [Releases](https://github.com/elhenro/bee/releases): version history and prebuilt binaries

## Install

- Install script: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/elhenro/bee/main/install.sh | sh`
- Go install: `go install github.com/elhenro/bee/cmd/bee@latest` (Go 1.26+)
- Prebuilt binaries for macOS and Linux (amd64, arm64) are on the releases page. Windows is untested.
- After installation, run `bee` and use `/model` to select a runtime and model. Local options include oMLX and Ollama; OpenRouter is available for hosted models.

## What it is

- Coding agent: writes code, runs tests, commits changes
- Pure Go: single static binary, no runtime dependencies
- Skills: `bee <name>` subcommands, one binary, one PATH entry
- Works everywhere: Ollama and oMLX local, OpenRouter hosted, tiny models to frontier
- No profiles: every model gets the same defaults. Lower the budgets in `~/.bee/config.toml` for a small context window
- Roles: worker (default), scout (read-only research and web), queen (a hive of workers). Cycle with shift+tab
- Parallel work: `bee agents` (one git worktree per task), `bee swarm`, `bee fan`
- Overnight loop: `bee zzz` makes one small change per iteration, then commits or rolls back
- Review aids: `bee explain` and `bee quiz` show what each request changed and why
- Procedure memory: a repeated read-only route becomes a replayable shortcut (a waggle)

## Local LLMs

- For local inference, use [Ollama](https://ollama.com) or [oMLX](https://github.com/jundot/omlx). oMLX supports Apple Silicon acceleration and prompt caching on macOS.
- My reference setup uses Qwen3.8-27B (oQ4e, ~17 GB, multi-token prediction) on a MacBook M3 Max with 64 GB RAM and oMLX. Sampling settings: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20.
